title: Protect time for sleep in a busy schedule
content: Busy schedules can squeeze out sleep. NHLBI advises setting aside enough time for sleep to protect health and daytime functioning.
source_locator: Opening paragraphs; text anchors: Sleep is often the first thing that busy people squeeze out of their schedules

observable_conditions: Repeatedly shortened sleep opportunity or sleep duration
required_context: A schedule constraint is needed to attribute the shortage to busyness
non_applicable_conditions: No evidence of insufficient sleep

title: A familiar short sleep routine is not proof of adaptation
content: NHLBI rejects the idea that people can learn to thrive on little sleep without adverse effects. A stable short routine does not by itself establish that sleep needs are met.
source_locator: Final paragraph about a common myth; text anchors: people can learn to get by on little sleep

observable_conditions: Sleep is consistently short even without a new decline
non_applicable_conditions: Sleep duration is sufficient for the applicable age group

title: Persistent insomnia symptoms can warrant professional review
content: On its insomnia page, NHS advises seeing a GP if changing sleeping habits has not helped insomnia, if sleeping difficulties have lasted months, or if insomnia makes daily life difficult to cope with. A two-week wearable window alone cannot establish these conditions.
source_locator: Non-urgent advice: See a GP if; text anchors: you've had trouble sleeping for months

observable_conditions: Reported sleeping difficulties or insomnia symptoms
required_context: Months-long sleeping difficulties, or insomnia with failed habit changes or substantial daily-life impact
non_applicable_conditions: Only a brief duration record without reported problems

title: Keep bedtime and waking time consistent
content: NHLBI recommends going to bed and waking at the same times each day. Changing sleep times repeatedly is a reason to review routine consistency, independently of total sleep hours.
source_locator: Sleep habit bullet list; text anchors: Go to bed and wake up at the same time every day

observable_conditions: Repeated variability in bedtime or wake time
non_applicable_conditions: A stable schedule alone does not establish a problem

title: Limit weeknight and weekend schedule differences
content: NHLBI advises keeping weeknight and weekend sleep schedules similar, with differences around an hour or less. Sleeping much later on weekends can disturb the sleep-wake rhythm.

required_context: Calendar grouping does not itself establish workdays
non_applicable_conditions: Weekday and weekend sleep times are similar

title: Repeated lost sleep can accumulate
content: NHLBI explains that regularly getting less sleep than needed adds up over time. The duration and recurrence of shortened nights matter; a current improvement does not quantify a complete recovery.

observable_conditions: Several shortened nights rather than a single isolated reading
non_applicable_conditions: Claiming a fixed number of recovery nights

title: Keep regular hours after a bad night

title: Insomnia duration categories require a symptom history
content: NHS distinguishes short-term insomnia lasting under three months from long-term insomnia lasting at least three months. The distinction requires a symptom history, not just fourteen days of short sleep estimates.

observable_conditions: Reported sleeping difficulties with known duration
required_context: Symptom history and onset
non_applicable_conditions: Diagnosing insomnia from estimated sleep hours

title: Estimated time asleep is different from the full sleep period
content: Google estimates time asleep from the portions of the main sleep period classified as light, deep, or REM sleep. Recorded bedtime-to-wake duration need not equal estimated minutes asleep.
